t: The Secretary may authorize the expenditure or transfer (within each bureau or office) of any appropriation in this title, in addition to the amounts included in the budget programs of the several agencies, for the suppression or emergency prevention of forest or range fires on or threatening lands under jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior.

fable.w: This section only authorizes the Secretary to spend or transfer appropriations within bureaus or offices for fire suppression and emergency prevention on Interior lands. The tempting reading is that authorizing a federal action implies some coordination, but the text names no state, tribe, local government, expert, or member of the public and requires no rulemaking, hearing, or consultation. Every actor is inside the federal government, so it is not participation.

opus.w: This section only lets the Secretary spend or move appropriated money within each bureau or office to fight or prevent forest and range fires. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is involved in that decision. The mention of fires threatening Interior lands does not bring in any outside party or require any consultation, hearing, comment period or rulemaking.
opus.s: The Secretary may authorize the expenditure or transfer (within each bureau or office) of any appropriation in this title
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** fire suppression on lands "threatening" Interior lands could seem to involve nearby states or landowners. That reading fails because the section only lets the Secretary spend or move money inside the Department. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of the Interior authority to spend appropriated funds for fire suppression. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). The only actors involved are the Secretary and internal bureaus/offices.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary may authorize the expenditure or transfer (within each bureau or office) of any appropriation in this title, in addition to the amounts included in the budget programs of the several agencies, for the suppression or emergency prevention of forest or range fires on or threatening lands under jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "emergency prevention" implies coordination with local authorities or the public, but the text itself only grants authority to the Secretary to spend funds. It does not mandate any specific interaction with outside parties. The actors mentioned are the Secretary and the bureaus/offices within the Department of the Interior, which are all inside the federal government.
